terminal_findings.mechanism: Normalization or reviewed equivalence can classify independently actionable impacts as one material failure.
terminal_findings.precondition: Two occurrences share an axis and mechanism ID but have materially distinct observable impacts.
terminal_findings.event: Normalization produces the same failure identity, or review approves equivalence without validated material-equivalence and consumer-closure semantics.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: The settled view counts the distinct impacts as one finding.
terminal_findings.falsifier: Verified cases show that same-identity impacts always form one closure unit, or that all consumers preserve distinct prioritization and closure despite deduplication.

terminal_findings.mechanism: A cross-revision merge could ignore changed handler effects while retaining the mechanism ID.
terminal_findings.precondition: H0 and H1 share the axis, mechanism ID, and failure identity.
terminal_findings.event: The handler changes from suppressed publication with automatic retry to provisional publication with manual triage and no retry.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Materially distinct operational outcomes are collapsed into one settled finding.
terminal_findings.falsifier: The typed all-known/all-equal revision predicate and negative H0-to-H1 conformance test keep the outcomes distinct.

terminal_findings.mechanism: Historical projections may be unreproducible if referenced policy artifacts, serialization rules, or epoch data are unavailable.
terminal_findings.precondition: Normalization or revision policy changes across view epochs.
terminal_findings.event: Rollback or replay attempts to reconstruct an earlier view without verified immutable artifacts and retention guarantees.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Previously published membership, statuses, totals, reasons, or effective timestamps cannot be reproduced.
terminal_findings.falsifier: A retained-artifact v1-to-v2-to-rollback replay byte-matches the canonical historical projection.

terminal_findings.mechanism: The general RevisionSemantics schema may omit a decision-relevant operational obligation.
terminal_findings.precondition: Two revisions differ in an unmodeled obligation while every modeled field matches.
terminal_findings.event: The all-known/all-equal predicate evaluates only the modeled fields.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Materially distinct revision outcomes may be classified as duplicates.
terminal_findings.falsifier: Schema-completeness evidence and negative mutation cases demonstrate coverage of all decision-relevant obligations.

limitations: The closed-world record contains no validated material-equivalence or downstream consumer-closure evidence for FINDING-1.
General revision-schema completeness remains unproven for FINDING-4.
Historical replay, immutable retention, canonical serialization, timestamp integrity, and artifact-recovery evidence are missing for FINDING-3.
Thread freshness and isolation are supported by separate fresh-thread setup and routed-input boundaries, not by claims of cognitive independence.
